title: How many public EV chargers will a city need?
prompt: A US city of one million people wants to plan its public electric-vehicle charging network. The mayor asks: how many public charging points will the city need in five years? Estimate the number and explain how you got there.

facts.answer: The city has 1,000,000 residents living in 400,000 households. Assume the number of households stays the same.
In five years, 10% of households will own an electric vehicle. Assume one EV per owning household.
70% of EV-owning households can charge at home. The other 30% cannot, for example because they live in apartments without a parking space, and rely on public chargers.
Count only residents' EVs. Ignore visitors, commuters from outside the city, taxis and delivery fleets.
Estimate the need five years from now, not today.
Public chargers are either Level 2 (slow, used for longer stops) or DC fast (quick top-ups). Ask for details on how demand splits between them and how many EVs one charger can support.
60% of public charging is done at Level 2 chargers and 40% at DC fast chargers. One Level 2 charger supports about 10 EVs that rely on public charging. One DC fast charger supports about 40.
The mayor wants public charging to be available so that an EV owner without home charging rarely has to wait.
Ignore downtime and maintenance in the base estimate. You may mention it as a risk.

key_buckets: From population to households to EV owners
Who cannot charge at home (the public-charging users)
How those drivers charge: charger type and frequency
Capacity: how many users one charger supports
good_signs: States each assumption clearly and checks it with the interviewer
Rounds numbers to keep the maths simple
Splits the problem into demand (who needs public charging) and supply (what each charger can serve)
Sanity-checks the answer, for example chargers per 1,000 residents
red_flags: Forgets that most EV owners can charge at home
Gives a number without any sense-check

exhibits.title: Public charger types
exhibits.reveal_hint: Ask how public charging demand splits between charger types and how many EVs each type supports.
exhibits.insight: Level 2 chargers make up most of the count (720 of 840), while DC fast chargers carry 40% of the demand with only 120 units.

math.question: How many EVs will the city have in five years?
How many of those EVs rely on public charging?
How many Level 2 chargers are needed?
math.working: 60% of 12,000 is 7,200 EVs using Level 2. At 10 EVs per charger that is 720 chargers.

math.question: How many DC fast chargers are needed?
math.working: 40% of 12,000 is 4,800 EVs using DC fast. At 40 EVs per charger that is 120 chargers.

math.question: How many public chargers does the city need in total?
math.working: 720 Level 2 plus 120 DC fast is 840 chargers, or about 0.84 per 1,000 residents.

brainstorm.question: What could make the real number of chargers needed higher or lower than your estimate, and what would you do about it?
idea_bank: Faster EV adoption than 10%, for example from incentives or falling prices
More residents able to charge at home after apartment parking retrofits, which lowers demand
Longer vehicle range, which means less frequent charging
Visitors, commuters and tourists adding demand
Taxi, ride-hailing and delivery fleets using public chargers heavily
Workplace charging reducing the need for public chargers
Charger downtime and maintenance raising the number needed
Grid capacity limits in some neighbourhoods
Pricing and time-of-day rules shifting when people charge

must_mention: A final estimate of about 800 to 900 chargers, roughly 720 Level 2 and 120 DC fast
The key assumptions: 10% adoption and 30% without home charging
A sense-check or sensitivity, such as what happens if adoption is 15%
good_signs: Gives a range as well as a point estimate
Suggests how to validate (pilot data, utility records, comparable cities)

model_answer_outline: Structure the estimate as demand (EV owners who need public charging) divided by supply (EVs one charger can serve), split by charger type.
Households: 1,000,000 residents in 400,000 households; 10% own an EV, so 40,000 EVs.
Public-charging need: 30% cannot charge at home, so 12,000 EVs rely on public chargers.
Split by type: 60% of charging is Level 2 (7,200 EVs at 10 per charger is 720 chargers); 40% is DC fast (4,800 EVs at 40 per charger is 120 chargers).
Total: about 840 public chargers, or roughly 0.84 per 1,000 residents. Sense-check against how many chargers are visible per neighbourhood.
Sensitivities: adoption (15% would make it about 1,260), home-charging share, and fleets or visitors. Recommend phasing the build with usage data every year.
